Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Yellow fever, unspecified. Year: 2026. ISO3: BFA. DON refs: DON2957. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: A condition caused by an infection with yellow fever virus. This condition is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, conjunctival congestion, or relative bradycardia. Severe conditions may also present with increasing fever, jaundice, renal failure, or bleeding. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is by detection of IgM anti-yellow fever virus antibodies in a serum sample.

ISO3: BGD. DON refs: DON2946. ICD: B00-B09. Definition: A disease of the respiratory system, caused by an infection with Morbillivirus. This disease is characterised by a blotchy rash, fever, cough, conjunctivitis, or malaise. This disease may also present with tiny white spots with bluish-white centres inside the mouth. Transmission is by inhalation of infected respiratory secretions, airborne transmission or direct contact. Confirmation is by detection of Morbillivirus RNA or measles-specific IgM antibodies.

Definition: A disease caused by an infection with Middle East Respiratory Syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoA). Confirmation is by identification of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome coronavirus from genetic material.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Diphtheria, unspecified. Year: 2025. ISO3: DZA. DON refs: DON2934. ICD: A30-A49. Definition: A disease commonly of the respiratory system, caused by an infection of the gram-positive bacteria Corynebacterium diphtheriae. This disease is characterised by sore throat, fever, and a pseudomembrane on the tonsils, pharynx, or nasal cavity. Transmission is by inhalation of infected respiratory secretions, or direct cutaneous contact. Confirmation is by identification of Corynebacterium diphtheriae from a throat swab or infected tissue, and by clinical signs.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Rift Valley fever. Year: 2025. ISO3: MRT. DON refs: DON2932. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: A disease caused by an infection with Rift Valley fever virus. This disease is commonly asymptomatic. This disease may also present with fever, liver abnormalities, weakness, back pain, or dizziness. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is commonly by detection of Rift Valley fever virus specific IgM or IgG antibodies in a blood sample.

Disease: Chikungunya mosquito-borne viral fever. Year: 2025. ISO3: USA. DON refs: DON2931. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: Individuals are infected with the virus through a mosquito bite from Aedes mosquitos (Aedes albopictus and A. aegypti). Concomitant fever and arthalgia are a common specific sign although infection can present with non-specific symptoms that can be confused with Dengue including headache, rash and myalgia. Disease: Malaria due to Plasmodium falciparum, unspecified. Year: 2024. ISO3: COD. DON refs: DON2899. ICD: B50-B64. Definition: A disease caused by an infection with the protozoan parasite Plasmodium falciparum. This disease is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, arthralgia, weakness, vomiting, or diarrhoea. This disease may also present with splenomegaly, anaemia, thrombocytopenia, hypoglycaemia, pulmonary or renal dysfunction, or neurologic changes. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is by identification of Plasmodium falciparum in a blood sample.

ISO3: SSD. DON refs: DON2794. ICD: B00-B09. Definition: A disease of the respiratory system, caused by an infection with Morbillivirus. This disease is characterised by a blotchy rash, fever, cough, conjunctivitis, or malaise. This disease may also present with tiny white spots with bluish-white centres inside the mouth. Transmission is by inhalation of infected respiratory secretions, airborne transmission or direct contact. Confirmation is by detection of Morbillivirus RNA or measles-specific IgM antibodies.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Ebola disease. Year: 2023. ISO3: UGA. DON refs: DON2788. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: A severe disease with high case fatality caused by infection with Ebola virus or a closely related virus. Ebola disease is typically characterised by acute onset of fever with non-specific symptoms/signs (e.g., abdominal pain, anorexia, fatigue, malaise, myalgia, sore throat) usually followed several days later by nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, and occasionally a variable rash. Hiccups may occur. Severe illness may include haemorrhagic manifestations (e.g., bleeding from puncture sites, ecchymoses

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Acute poliomyelitis, unspecified. Year: 2023. ISO3: SDN. DON refs: DON2787. ICD: A80-A89. Definition: A disease of the nervous system, caused by human poliovirus. This disease commonly presents with a fever, sore throat, headache, vomiting, or stiffness of the neck and back. This disease may present with an acute onset of flaccid paralysis. Transmission is commonly by the faecal-oral route or direct contact. Confirmation is by identification of poliovirus in a faecal sample or by a lumbar puncture.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Yellow fever, unspecified. Year: 2023. ISO3: CMR. DON refs: DON2786. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: A condition caused by an infection with yellow fever virus. This condition is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, conjunctival congestion, or relative bradycardia. Severe conditions may also present with increasing fever, jaundice, renal failure, or bleeding. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is by detection of IgM anti-yellow fever virus antibodies in a serum sample.

Disease: Acute poliomyelitis, unspecified. Year: 2022. ISO3: IDN. DON refs: DON2785. ICD: A80-A89. Definition: A disease of the nervous system, caused by human poliovirus. This condition is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, conjunctival congestion, or relative bradycardia. Severe conditions may also present with increasing fever, jaundice, renal failure, or bleeding. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is by detection of IgM anti-yellow fever virus antibodies in a serum sample.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Leptospirosis, unspecified. Year: 2022. ISO3: TZA. DON refs: DON2758. ICD: A20-A28. Definition: A disease caused by an infection with the gram-negative bacteria Leptospira. In the first phase, this disease is characterised by generalised illness (fever, chills, or myalgias) or individuals may be asymptomatic

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Acute viral hepatitis, unspecified. Year: 2022. ISO3: CAN. DON refs: DON2754, DON2751, DON2743. ICD: B15-B19. Definition: A group of liver diseases characterised by liver inflammation and fibrosis, caused by more than 6 months of infection with one or more of hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus and hepatitis D virus, with or without HIV. Even at stage of cirrhosis there are often no symptoms. Otherwise, clinical features include fatigue, hard liver edge and complications of cirrhosis (muscle wasting, ascites, splenomegaly/portal hypertension). Transmission of hepatitis B and C viruses is by blood and body fluid co

This condition is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, conjunctival congestion, or relative bradycardia. Confirmation is by detection of IgM anti-yellow fever virus antibodies in a serum sample.

Definition: Influenza, caused by influenza virus strains of special epidemiological importance with an animal-human or inter-human transmission.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Acute hepatitis E. Year: 2020. ISO3: BFA. DON refs: DON2667. ICD: B15-B19. Definition: A disease of the liver, caused by an acute infection with hepatitis E virus. This disease is characterised by nausea. Transmission is commonly by the faecal-oral route. Confirmation is by detection of anti-hepatitis E virus IgM antibodies in an individual's serum.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Measles. Year: 2020. ISO3: BDI. DON refs: DON2639. ICD: B00-B09. Definition: A disease of the respiratory system, caused by an infection with Morbillivirus. This disease is characterised by a blotchy rash, fever, cough, conjunctivitis, or malaise. This disease may also present with tiny white spots with bluish-white centres inside the mouth. Transmission is by inhalation of infected respiratory secretions, airborne transmission or direct contact. Confirmation is by detection of Morbillivirus RNA or measles-specific IgM antibodies.

Year: 2020. ISO3: CHN. DON refs: DON2600. ICD: J09-J18. Definition: A disease of the pulmonary system, caused by an infection with a viral source. Year: 2020. ISO3: COD. DON refs: DON2654. ICD: A20-A28. Definition: A disease caused by an infection with the gram-negative bacteria Yersinia pestis. This disease commonly presents with an infection of the lymph nodes leading to swelling and pain. This disease may also present with gangrene of the extremities, chills, malaise, high fever, muscle cramps, or seizures. Transmission is through the bite of an infected flea, by direct contact, or by droplet transmission.

Disease: Yellow fever, unspecified. Year: 2020. ISO3: ETH. DON refs: DON2633. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: A condition caused by an infection with yellow fever virus. This condition is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, conjunctival congestion, or relative bradycardia. Severe conditions may also present with increasing fever, jaundice, renal failure, or bleeding. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is by detection of IgM anti-yellow fever virus antibodies in a serum sample.

Year: 2020. ISO3: ETH. DON refs: DON2643. ICD: B65-B83. Definition: A disease resulting from drinking water contaminated with water fleas infected with larvae of the nematode Dracunculus medinensis. Disease: Oropouche virus disease. Year: 2020. ISO3: GUF. DON refs: DON2660. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: A disease caused by an infection with Oropouche virus. This disease is characterised by fever, headache, neck and back pain, joint pain, or photophobia. Confirmation is by detection of the Oropouche virus specific antibodies in a serum sample.

This condition is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, conjunctival congestion, or relative bradycardia. Severe conditions may also present with increasing fever, jaundice, renal failure, or bleeding. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is by detection of IgM anti-yellow fever virus antibodies in a serum sample.

Disease: Dengue fever, unspecified. Year: 2019. ISO3: AFG. DON refs: DON2592. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: Dengue is a viral disease transmitted by the bite of a mosquito infected by dengue viruses. It is one disease entity with different clinical presentations and often with unpredictable clinical evolution and outcome. Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Measles. Year: 2019. ISO3: ASM. DON refs: DON2583. ICD: B00-B09. Definition: A disease of the respiratory system, caused by an infection with Morbillivirus. This disease is characterised by a blotchy rash, fever, cough, conjunctivitis, or malaise. This disease may also present with tiny white spots with bluish-white centres inside the mouth. Transmission is by inhalation of infected respiratory secretions, airborne transmission or direct contact. Confirmation is by detection of Morbillivirus RNA or measles-specific IgM antibodies.

Disease: Acute poliomyelitis, unspecified. Year: 2019. ISO3: AGO. DON refs: DON2546. ICD: A80-A89. Definition: A disease of the nervous system, caused by human poliovirus. This disease commonly presents with a fever, sore throat, headache, vomiting, or stiffness of the neck and back. This disease may present with an acute onset of flaccid paralysis. Confirmation is by detection of IgM anti-yellow fever virus antibodies in a serum sample.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Yellow fever, unspecified. Year: 2009. ISO3: LBR. DON refs: DON1388. ICD: A92-A99. Definition: A condition caused by an infection with yellow fever virus. This condition is characterised by fever, chills, headache, myalgia, conjunctival congestion, or relative bradycardia. Severe conditions may also present with increasing fever, jaundice, renal failure, or bleeding. Transmission is through the bite of an infected mosquito. Confirmation is by detection of IgM anti-yellow fever virus antibodies in a serum sample.

disease: Whooping cough due to Bordetella pertussis
text: Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Whooping cough due to Bordetella pertussis. Year: 2003. ISO3: AFG. DON refs: DON0655, DON0653. ICD: A30-A49. Definition: A disease of the upper respiratory tract, caused by an infection of the gram-negative bacteria Bordetella pertussis. This disease typically presents with paroxysmal cough, inspiratory whoop, and fainting or vomiting after coughing. Transmission is by inhalation of infected respiratory secretions. Confirmation is by identification of Bordetella pertussis from nasopharyngeal samples or sputum, or detection of antibodies against Bordetella pertussis.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Diphtheria, unspecified. Year: 2003. ISO3: AFG. DON refs: DON0785. ICD: A30-A49. Definition: A disease commonly of the respiratory system, caused by an infection of the gram-positive bacteria Corynebacterium diphtheriae. This disease is characterised by sore throat, fever, and a pseudomembrane on the tonsils, pharynx, or nasal cavity. Transmission is by inhalation of infected respiratory secretions, or direct cutaneous contact. Confirmation is by identification of Corynebacterium diphtheriae from a throat swab or infected tissue, and by clinical signs.

Country-year outbreak record from the Global Pandemic and Epidemic-Prone Disease Outbreaks dataset (HDX / Torres Munguía et al., derived from WHO Disease Outbreak News). Disease: Plague, unspecified. Year: 2003. ISO3: DZA. DON refs: DON0774, DON0765, DON0777. ICD: A20-A28. Definition: A disease caused by an infection with the gram-negative bacteria Yersinia pestis. This disease commonly presents with an infection of the lymph nodes leading to swelling and pain. This disease may also present with gangrene of the extremities, chills, malaise, high fever, muscle cramps, or seizures. Transmission is through the bite of an infected flea, by direct contact, or by droplet transmission.
